body.p: Claims 2-11 are pending and claims 2-10 stand rejected by the Office Action of

December 17, 2024. This Response amends claims 2-10 and adds new claim 11. The claim amendments and added claim add no new matter. For example, support for the claim amendments may be found in paragraphs [0046] and [0073]. Applicant respectfully requests reexamination and reconsideration of pending claims 2-11.

With this paper, Figures 10-13 are being replaced with Figures 10-13 on the attached Replacement Sheets. In Figures 10-13, the reference numeral 216 is being replaced with the reference numeral 220. No new matter is added. Applicant respectfully requests entry of amended Figures 10-13.

Claim 2 is rejected on the ground of non-statutory double patenting, as allegedly being unpatentable over claim 1 of U.S. Patent No. 12,004,884, in view of Barnes et al. (U.S. 2016/0081710). Applicant will address any future non-statutory double patenting rejection, if one may be applied to the currently amended claims.

Claims 2 and 4-10 stand rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103, as allegedly being unpatentable over U.S. Patent Publication 2016/0081710 ("Barnes"), in view of U.S. Patent Publication 2004/0034276 ("Voellmicke"). Claim 3 stands rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103, as allegedly being unpatentable over Barnes and Voellmicke and further in view of U.S. Patent Publication 2007/0213616 ("Anderson"). Applicant respectfully traverses these rejections.
As currently amended, claim 2 is directed to a method for cutting a transverse carpal

ligament. The method includes steps of activating a locking mechanism on the balloon activation lever to lock the two balloons in an inflated state and unlocking the locking mechanism. The cited Barnes, Voellmicke, and Anderson references all fail to teach or suggest at least the step of activating a locking mechanism on the balloon activation lever to lock the two balloons in an

inflated state. Although Barnes does teach a locked position and an unlocked position, he does not teach the specific method step of activating a locking mechanism on the balloon activation lever to lock the two balloons in an inflated state. Therefore, even if Barnes and Voellmicke could be combined, the method of claim 2 would not be achieved. Anderson does not remedy this shortcoming and is not relevant to claim 2.

At least for these reasons, Applicant respectfully submits that claim 2 and all dependent claims are patentable over Barnes, Voellmicke, and Anderson. Applicant thus respectfully requests withdrawal of the rejections of claims 2-10 under 35 U.S.C. § 103.

Examination of the elected claims is respectfully requested. It is respectfully submitted that all pending claims are now in condition for allowance. Issuance of a Notice of Allowance in due course is also respectfully requested. If a telephone conference might be of assistance, please contact the undersigned attorney at (612) 677-9050.
